text:
Priya: @team customer Finata reports ~120 objects that hit TTL (30d) yesterday but are still searchable in the product UI. They provided object IDs and a repro curl. Can someone triage?

Alex: taking this. Can you paste the object IDs and the original retention policy change history?

Priya: pasted IDs in thread + policy change timeline. We switched the tenant from default-30d -> custom-90d on 2026-02-10 then back to default-30d on 2026-03-15 via API. Customer says they expected deletion after 30d from original ingestion, not policy change date.

Jordan: quick checklist: 1) Verify deletion-job logs for that tenant 2) Check KMS audit for any decrypt errors during delete 3) Confirm audit logs show a delete event emitted to storage.

Megan: pinging infra-bot to pull deletion-queue status and last-run logs for tenant finata-prod.

infra-bot: deletion-queue:fetch --tenant finata-prod --since 2026-03-14
infra-bot: RESULTS: 121 items in queue, last run: 2026-03-15T21:12:03Z, status: partially_failed (23 failures).

Alex: failures -> show sample failure log pls (sanitized).

infra-bot: sample-failure (ID: obj-312) 
```
ERROR 2026-03-15T21:12:03Z delete_worker: delete failed for obj-312: storage_api: PutObject failed: AccessDenied (KMS:Decrypt) key:projects/finata/kms/primary
stack: github.com/redwood/inference/storage.DeleteObject -> storage_client.go:142
```

Jordan: KMS AccessDenied on delete is red flag — if object is encrypted with customer-managed key and we rotated policy or lacked permission, delete cannot proceed because we need to read/verify the object metadata before final removal.

Priya: customer says they did not change KMS policy. They are on Redwood-managed key but tied to a HSM gateway we updated. Could that cause transient AccessDenied?

Megan: yes, we pushed an HSM gateway upgrade on 2026-03-15 21:05 UTC (release 2.4.1). There was a short window where the gateway rejected old-signed requests. That aligns with the delete job failure window.

Alex: hypothesis: deletion job tried during gateway upgrade -> KMS errors -> items stayed in deletion-queue. When policy changed (30d->90d->30d) timestamps might have been recomputed causing ambiguity re: original TTL anchor. Need to confirm time-of-ingest vs policy-change anchors.

Jordan: repro steps for eng to validate:
1) pick one object ID that failed (obj-312)
2) run internal delete simulation: `internal-cli delete-sim --tenant finata-prod --id obj-312 --dry-run` to observe KMS handshake
3) query deletion-queue table: `SELECT id, status, last_error, last_attempt FROM deletion_queue WHERE tenant='finata-prod' AND id='obj-312';`
4) fetch audit log: `auditctl get --tenant finata-prod --event delete --id obj-312 --json`

Priya: pasted sample outputs from customer curl and our UI request id: req_0a7c. They also attached screenshots that show objects still listed under search results.

Megan: ran step 3 locally: 
```
id      | status          | last_error                          | last_attempt
obj-312 | failed          | KMS:AccessDenied                    | 2026-03-15T21:12:03Z
obj-413 | pending         | NULL                                | 2026-03-15T21:12:03Z
```

Alex: ran delete-sim (step 2) with debug flag — shows KMS handshake failing with HSM gateway returning 403 for Decrypt request. Stack traces point to gateway version mismatch.

infra-bot: gateway-release: 2.4.1 applied to cluster a, rollout started 2026-03-15T20:58Z, completed 2026-03-15T21:20Z. ~22min window with increased 5xx/403 to KMS proxy observed.

Jordan: mitigation plan:
- Clear backlog: requeue failed deletion items for tenant finata-prod with exponential backoff, but ensure KMS stable.
- For items that still show as 'searchable' we should run force-delete once KMS allows (requires operator auth).
- Add a graceful-fallback to mark delete as 'deferred' with audit note rather than leave in failed state indefinitely.

Megan: I'll kick a requeue for that tenant now and monitor. Requeue command: `deletionctl requeue --tenant finata-prod --filter 'status=failed' --note "post-hsm-upgrade-retry"`

Alex: also need to patch the deletion worker to record the ingestion timestamp in the deletion record and keep original TTL anchor if policy changes happen — prevents policy-change from resetting expectations. Filing a quick PR: storage:keep-ingest-anchor.

Priya: customer update: told them we identified KMS gateway upgrade as likely root cause, currently retrying deletes and will confirm when objects are removed. They want ETA.

Jordan: ETA: requeue + one delete run should clear most items within 1-2 hours assuming gateway healthy. If many items still fail due to key perms we'll need KMS team to investigate key ACLs.

Megan: requeue started at 2026-03-16T01:08Z. infra-bot shows progress: 121 -> 98 -> 52 items remaining. continuing. :eyes:

Priya: customer asked if retention metrics (audit logs) will show that deletion was attempted earlier. We should surface failed attempts in the audit UI.

Alex: action items:
- Megan: finish requeue + confirm removal (in scope: force-delete if necessary) (ETA 2h)
- Jordan: add audit-ui ticket to surface failed deletion attempts and KMS error codes (ETA 1 sprint)
- Alex: open PR to keep ingest anchor for TTL (ETA EOD)
- Priya: keep customer updated every 2 hours until confirm

Megan: update 2026-03-16T02:20Z: all 121 items reprocessed, 4 still in failed state (manual followup required). Will request KMS key ACL check for the 4.

Priya: closing loop: customer confirmed 117 objects removed from UI, will escalate if they still see residuals. Thanks team. :thanks:

Alex: retrospective note: avoid rolling KMS/HSM gateway during mass deletion jobs or add a short maintenance flag that pauses deletion workers. Filing ops playbook update.

Jordan: added temporary monitor to alert on >5% deletion-job failures inside 1h window post-gateway-release.

Megan: any other ask from support?

Priya: none for now, will reopen if customer sees more.

infra-bot: NOTE: internal ticket STORAGE-3482 created for requeue + telemetry improvements.
